events.preview_text: Use email.delivered as a separate signal for transactional email.
events.body:
Resend lets you inspect a delivery event after a transactional email is sent. Start with `email.delivered` to see a concrete signal beyond the send response.

Resend webhooks send real-time email events as JSON POST requests to an endpoint you control. That separates the request to send from the event reporting what happened next, without treating delivery as proof of inbox placement, message opening, or end-user receipt.

The documented first step is to register a publicly accessible endpoint and select `email.delivered`. The guide shows how Resend sends the event payload to your route, so you can evaluate whether that signal fits your transactional-email workflow.

events.subject: Inspect the event after send
events.preview_text: Use `email.delivered` as a separate signal for transactional email.
events.body:
A send response covers the send request. Inspecting what happens next requires a separate delivery signal.

Resend webhooks send real-time email lifecycle events as JSON POST requests to an endpoint you control. Start with `email.delivered` to inspect a concrete event after a transactional email is sent.

The documented first step is to register a publicly accessible endpoint and select `email.delivered`. When that event arrives, your route receives a JSON payload with its details.

That signal is distinct from the send response. It does not establish inbox placement, an open, or end-user receipt, but it gives you a delivery event you can inspect at your own endpoint.

Read the webhook guide and review the first setup step.
